newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end Tokyo sharply up but off record highs.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end Tokyo sharply up but off record highs.

text.p: The key March 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract closed sharply higher on Monday, but down slightly from a record high for any benchmark contract of 126.83, hit earlier in the day.
The key contract jumped after a round of speculative buying buoyed SIMEX trade during the Tokyo lunch break. Short-covering continued as the contract broke above key resistance points.
"The market was driven by day-to-day dealing," said a senior dealer at a major brokerage house. "Operators here were mostly unhappy about the rises before tomorrow's bond auction."
The March ended at 126.70, up 0.48 from Friday's close.
A total of 43,854 contracts changed hands.

Tokyo operators were hesitant to buy on Monday because higher prices would result in a lower coupon rate for 10-year JGBs to be auctioned on Tuesday, traders said. The last auction of 10-year JGBs carried a record-low 2.7 percent coupon.
But after Tokyo's morning close, the March exceeded Tokyo's morning high of 126.38 and set a record high of 126.70 on the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX).
Traders here said that the buying spree in Singapore was led by speculative operations by a few U.S. major brokerage firms and a U.S. futures trading firm.
There was also a rumour that a major Japanese bank had suffered large losses in derivatives trading and is now covering short positions in JGBs, traders said.
The rumour could not be immediately confirmed.

Short-squeezing after a break above key resistance points of 126.40 and 126.70 in afternoon trade gave the March additional momentum. A lack of investors' participation ahead of the auction was another support, traders said.
"No profit-taking was detected from investors today. They had been active sellers when the key contract rose to 126.30-126.40," said a dealer at another major brokerage house.
In the cash market, falls in bond yields were relatively small, traders said. The yield of key 182nd 10-year JGBs stood at 2.350 percent at 0727 GMT, down 0.050 from Friday's close.

"A speculative buying in JGB futures on SIMEX was related to selling in TOPIX stock index futures," said a long-term credit bank dealer. "But that had nothing to do with the cash market, where operators were concerned about the bond auction and the amount of JGB holdings before the book closings," he said, adding that the key bond yield may be underpinned at the record low for any benchmark of 3.330 percent for now. -- Risa Maeda, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8570
